title: HelpCenter — Pick a Page
objective: The help center loads article content by name from a templates directory. Make it load a file that was never meant to be an article.

verifier.condition: The rendered help page includes the content of a file outside the templates directory, located via the page parameter.

weakness: A page name is used to build a template path with no check that the resolved path stays inside the templates directory, so a crafted name can include and render an unrelated file's content inline.
vulnerableEndpoint: GET /help?page= (joined onto the templates directory, rendered inline)
seededData: A simulated filesystem with several help templates and a sibling 'config' directory holding a synthetic application config file.
hints: Browse a couple of normal help pages and note exactly how 'page' maps to what's shown.
This behaves like a filename being looked up in a directory, not like a fixed set of known article IDs. What else lives near that directory?
The templates directory isn't the only thing on this simulated filesystem.
burpNotes: Enumerate the page parameter with traversal sequences pointing at sibling directories; the response renders whatever content is found directly inline.
